To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

normal intima tissue and atherosclerotic lesions from human coronary artery and aorta did differ in absolute or in relative triglyceride contents; that the relative triglyceride amount decreased in both aorta and coronary arteries with the development of lesions; and that the relative triglyceide content of lesions did not differ in the two anatomic sites.
the absolute and relative lipid content of normal intima, intracellular lipid lesions, and foam cell fatty streak lesions are similar.
the lipid composition of atherosclerosis does not change progressively as the disease progresses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical and morphological changes that occur in the intima of arteries as atherosclerosis develops.
the development of an animal model of the atherosclerotic plaque, which will allow the study of the pathogenesis of the plaque.
the development of an experimental model for the study of the lipid composition of the intima of normal arteries and of lesions from human coronary artery and human aorta.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
atherosclerosis is not associated with any specific alteration in lipid composition of the arterial intima.
atherogenesis does not appear to be a simple process.
atherosclerosis is not a disease of triglyceride metabolism and that cholesteryl esters are not a major constituent of atherosclerotic plaques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of intracellular lipid lesions, foam cell lesions, and fibrous plaques are not associated with a progressive change in lipid composition.
the formation of intracellular lipid lesions is associated with a decrease in relative triglyceride and an increase in relative cholesteryl esters.

the formation of intracellular lipid lesions, foam cell fatty streak, and fibrous plaques in coronary arteries and aortic intima is not associated with progressive increments in total lipid or with progressive changes in relative lipid composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fibrous plaques have a different lipid composition than intracellular lipid lesions, foam cell lesions, and fatty streaks.
there is a continuum of lipid composition of the intima of coronary arteries and aortas.
there is no evidence that the lipid composition of atherosclerosis lesions is related to their development.
